title: Outcome-Value Evaluation Framework
description: Evaluates AI systems on value delivery rather than interface quality. Based on Phil Gilbert's insight that with AI, design output is no longer performance - the focus must be on outcome value.

thought_leader.name: Phil Gilbert
thought_leader.role: Former Head of Design at IBM
thought_leader.key_insight: AI output is cheap, so designers must focus on the value and trust of AI actions, not interface polish

paradigm_shift.from: Evaluating interface quality (is the button discoverable?)
paradigm_shift.to: Evaluating outcome value (did the interaction improve the user's situation?)

principles.name: Value Clarity
principles.description: Is the outcome the system delivers clearly valuable to the user?
key_questions: Does the user's situation measurably improve after interaction?
Can the value delivered be articulated in user terms, not system terms?
Is the value persistent or ephemeral?
Would the user pay for this value (time, money, attention)?

questions: What specific user problem does this interaction solve?
How would the user describe the value they received?
Is the value immediately apparent or does it require explanation?
Does the value compound over multiple interactions?
what_to_look_for: Clear connection between interaction and user benefit
Value articulated in user language, not feature language
Evidence of real-world impact
Value that persists beyond the interaction
anti_patterns: Value described only in system terms (processed, optimized)
Value requires lengthy explanation to understand
Value disappears when user leaves the system
Value primarily benefits the system, not the user

metrics.name: outcome_achievement_rate
metrics.description: Percentage of interactions resulting in intended user outcome

metrics.name: value_articulation_clarity
metrics.description: Can users clearly state what value they received?
metrics.measurement: User interview: 'What did this help you accomplish?'

metrics.name: value_persistence
metrics.description: How long does the delivered value remain useful?
metrics.measurement: Time until value becomes stale or irrelevant

principles.name: Value Velocity
principles.description: How quickly does the system deliver value?
key_questions: What is the time from intent expression to value delivery?
How much user effort was required to extract value?
What is the ratio of interaction time to value received?
Are there unnecessary steps between intent and value?

questions: How many steps from user intent to value delivery?
What is the minimum viable interaction to achieve value?
Does the system front-load value or delay it?
Are there gratuitous interactions that don't add value?
what_to_look_for: Direct paths to value without unnecessary detours
Front-loaded value delivery
Minimal steps between intent and outcome
Progressive value delivery during longer interactions
anti_patterns: Value delayed until end of long interaction
Required steps that don't contribute to outcome
Engagement theater (activity without value)
Value hidden behind complexity

metrics.name: time_to_value
metrics.description: Elapsed time from first interaction to first value delivery

metrics.name: effort_to_value_ratio
metrics.description: User effort invested relative to value received

principles.name: Trust Calibration
principles.description: Does the user trust the system appropriately for the value it delivers?
key_questions: Does user trust match actual system reliability?
Are users appropriately skeptical of uncertain outputs?
Does the system help users verify value claims?
Is trust earned through demonstrated value, not claims?

questions: How does the system communicate its confidence level?
Can users verify AI outputs without redoing the work?
Does trust level match demonstrated capability?
Are high-stakes decisions appropriately flagged?
what_to_look_for: Confidence indicators that match actual reliability
Verification mechanisms that don't negate time savings
Trust built through track record, not assertion
Appropriate caution signals for uncertain outputs
anti_patterns: Overconfident presentation of uncertain outputs
No way to verify without redoing work
Trust demanded before demonstrated
Same confidence level for all outputs regardless of uncertainty

metrics.name: trust_calibration_accuracy
metrics.description: How well user trust matches actual system reliability

metrics.name: value_verification_ease
metrics.description: Effort to verify AI output vs effort to produce manually

principles.name: Value Compounding
principles.description: Does value accumulate over time and interactions?
key_questions: Does the system learn what's valuable to this user?
Does value delivery improve with continued use?
Is there compounding benefit from the relationship?
Does past value inform future value?

questions: Is the 10th interaction more valuable than the 1st?
Does the system remember user preferences and patterns?
Can accumulated context be leveraged for future value?
Is there a 'flywheel effect' where value begets more value?
what_to_look_for: Personalization that improves value over time
Learning from user feedback and corrections
Context accumulation that reduces future effort
Network effects where more use = more value
anti_patterns: Every interaction starts from zero
No memory of past preferences or patterns
Value plateaus regardless of usage
User must re-teach the system repeatedly

metrics.name: learning_effectiveness
metrics.description: Rate of improvement in value delivery over time
metrics.measurement: Value per interaction trend line slope

metrics.name: value_trajectory
metrics.description: Direction and magnitude of value change over time

principles.name: Value Transparency
principles.description: Can users understand how value was created?
key_questions: Is the source of value visible and verifiable?
Can users trace from output back to reasoning?
Is value attribution clear (AI vs user contribution)?
Can users learn to create similar value independently?

questions: How did the AI arrive at this valuable output?
What inputs/data contributed to this value?
Could the user have achieved this value differently?
What did the AI actually do vs what did the user do?
what_to_look_for: Explainable value creation process
Source attribution for key decisions
Clear AI/human contribution delineation
Learning opportunities for users
anti_patterns: Magic black box value creation
No explanation of how output was derived
Unclear what the AI actually contributed
User becomes dependent without understanding

metrics.name: value_explainability
metrics.description: Can users understand how value was created?
metrics.measurement: User can explain AI's contribution in own words

metrics.name: attribution_clarity
metrics.description: Clear understanding of AI vs user contribution
metrics.measurement: User accurately attributes who did what

evaluation_methodology.approach: Evaluate AI systems on value delivered, not interaction design
evaluation_methodology.key_shift: Ask 'What value did the user receive?' not 'Was the interface usable?'

steps.name: Define Value Outcomes
steps.description: Identify what specific user outcomes constitute 'value'
actions: Interview users about what success looks like
Distinguish between system value and user value

steps.name: Measure Value Delivery
steps.description: Assess whether and how value is delivered
actions: Measure time and effort to value

steps.name: Evaluate Trust Alignment
steps.description: Assess whether user trust matches system capability
actions: Compare user confidence to actual reliability

steps.name: Track Value Trajectory
actions: Compare early vs late interaction value

levels.label: Excellent Value
levels.description: Clear, immediate, persistent value that compounds over time

levels.label: Good Value
levels.description: Clear value delivered, minor improvements possible

levels.label: Adequate Value
levels.description: Value present but not optimized, room for improvement

levels.label: Poor Value
levels.description: Value unclear or significantly delayed, major improvements needed

levels.label: No Value
levels.description: No discernible user value or value negative (wasted time/effort)

when_to_use: Assessing whether AI investment is delivering ROI
Comparing AI solutions on value delivery
